sentences.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption surveyed suppliers about perceived corruption in state and local government procurement.
sentences.support: This research paper provides a picture of the extent of corruption from the perspective of suppliers

sentences.text: The online survey received 1,515 responses and examined overall perceptions, corruption-prone behaviour and vulnerability at different procurement stages.
sentences.support: a total of 1,515 responses were received by the ICAC.

sentences.text: The Commission reports that about two-fifths of suppliers saw corruption as at least a moderate problem, and almost one-third had avoided bidding because of corruption concerns.
sentences.support: almost one-third of suppliers indicated that they had declined to bid on a government contract because of corruption concerns.

sentences.text: The Commission concludes that these perceptions require attention even if inaccurate because they can affect suppliers’ willingness to compete.
sentences.support: Consequently, the need to address these perceptions applies even if they are inaccurate.

findings.quote: Overall, these results indicate that the supplier base of NSW state and local government procurement is concerned about corruption.

notes: Survey perceptions and suppliers’ reported behaviour are not findings of particular corrupt acts. No formal recommendations list. The executive summary says about two-fifths while the conclusion uses nearly half for the broad prevalence perception.
